RQA detects pharmacologically induced autononomic changes in the isolated rat cardiac signals.
RQA can be applied to the continuous cardiac signal to detect changes in autonomic tone in the isolated rat.
RQA of the cardiac signal can be used to detect pharmacologically induced alterations in cardiac variability.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of an objective, quantitative method for detecting changes in cardiac variability in the presence of autonomic nervous system (ANS) activity.
the development and evaluation of a new technique to detect changes in the dynamics of cardiac variability.
the development of a novel technique for the analysis of heart rate variability (HRV).

RQA can detect changes in cardiac variability in the isolated heart.
RQA can be used to assess cardiac variability, but that it may be more sensitive to the presence of autonomic imbalance than to the inherent variability of the isolated rat heart.
RQA is a promising technique for assessing autonomic changes in cardiac variability.

the dynamics underlying the continuous LVP or electrographic signal from an isolated rat model can be altered with pharmacological manipulation of the autonomic division of the nervous system.

nonlinear techniques may be used to detect changes in cardiac variability in the presence of pharmacologically induced autoregulation.
